A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AdaBet and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. The complete documents, including v2's Appendices A–E, support comparison; substantial material was relocated rather than removed.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification, memory, timing, and ablation results, including Tables 3–4 and Figures 6–12.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds isolated-layer accuracy, channel-selection, baseline-comparison, and Raspberry Pi results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: V1 selects whole layers and identifies finer selection granularity as future work. V2 Section 4.2.4 introduces a second stage that ranks channels within selected layers using normalized Betti numbers and selects a proportion rho_ch. This changes the trainable parameter subset while retaining the original layer-selection procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-pretrained models and the same four downstream image-classification datasets: Stanford Dogs, Oxford-IIIT Pets, CUB, and Flowers102. The added analyses retain this data and task coverage; Raspberry Pi evaluation changes execution hardware and measurement procedures.

E2.justification: V2 adds Last-K-Layers to the corresponding accuracy and memory comparisons in Tables 2–3 while retaining all five earlier baselines. Figure D.15 also adds Last-K-Layers and Fisher Information comparisons to the layer-budget analysis, which previously examined AdaBet alone.

E3.justification: The original benchmark settings are retained, but v2 adds isolated-layer training, channel-fraction sweeps, and comparisons across matched layer-selection fractions. Appendix E introduces Raspberry Pi evaluation with batch size 2, rho=0.1, rho_ch=1.0, total CPU-process memory measurement, and CPU utilization, extending the evaluation design beyond the original GPU experiments.

E4.justification: V2 Figure 2 adds isolated-layer accuracy to investigate whether Betti scores identify useful layers. Figure 7 and Appendix D.6 test channel-selection tradeoffs, while Appendix D.7 compares budget controllability against heuristic and Fisher selection. Earlier normalization, batch-size, accumulation, and training-stage analyses remain in Appendix D.

E5.justification: Both versions report three independent runs per main accuracy configuration and five runs for the Betti/clustering diagnostic, with graphical error bars. V2 extends that diagnostic with accuracy results using the same reporting practice; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence interval, or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Existing main-table scores remain unchanged, including AdaBet's 76.26% average, while v2 adds Last-K-Layers results averaging 73.75%, isolated-layer accuracy, channel-selection results, and CPU measurements. Appendix E reports memory reductions of 20.6% and 6.2% versus full training for ResNet50 and MobileNetV2. The layer-budget accuracy curve also changes between v1 Figure 10 and v2 Figure 7.

T1.justification: The homology definitions, chain-complex discussion, and Betti-number formula move to Appendix B without substantive mathematical revision. V2's labeled Definition 1 restates the existing first-Betti-number concept for layer activations; no new theorem, proof, or derivation is supplied.

C1.justification: V2 expands the central contribution from layer selection to layer-and-channel selection in the abstract, contributions, and conclusion. The abstract and Section 6.1 reduce the claimed average accuracy advantage from 5% to 2.5%, although the introduction and conclusion inconsistently retain 5%. The 40% average memory-reduction claim remains.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations connecting high Betti numbers to entangled, task-misaligned representations and similar channel scores to feature redundancy. It qualifies activation-size normalization and documents CPU profiling confounds and device limitations, while compressing v1's detailed discussion. Appendix D.7 also introduces a stronger interpretation of uniform accuracy–memory dominance that its plot does not consistently support.

D1.justification: V2 documents the 2GB Raspberry Pi 4, batch-size and selection settings, aggregate CPU profiling using the named 'psutils' library, and the absence of process isolation. Appendix C specifies how Last-K-Layers derives K from rho. Existing software versions, preprocessing, learning rates, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to 'Cache and reuse' for Last-K-Layers and 'Channel compression' for channel redundancy, and removes 'Tiny machine learning: Progress and futures.' The substantive positioning against TinyTrain, ElasticTrainer, and other prior methods is largely preserved, with detailed related work relocated to Appendix A.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes and condenses the narrative: detailed related work, topology background, implementation settings, and many experiments move to appendices. Learning-capacity motivation moves earlier, timing discussions merge, and the lengthy discussion section becomes a short conclusion and future-work summary. Extensive prose and author-block editing accompany this restructuring.

P2.justification: V2 removes v1's overview diagram while retaining its detailed pipeline, expands comparison tables for Last-K-Layers, and redraws the Betti diagnostic with an accuracy axis. Existing multipanel figures are split or rearranged across the main text and appendices, new channel and CPU plots are added, and captions, typography, and page layout are extensively reformatted.

improvement.justification: The added Last-K-Layers control and first device measurements strengthen evaluation, while channel selection addresses v1's stated granularity limitation. However, important new conclusions conflict with their evidence: Section 6.3.3 claims 74% memory savings with stable accuracy, whereas Figure 7 shows roughly 307 to 255 MB and 86.5% to 78% accuracy. Figure D.15 also contradicts universal dominance, and the 2.5% and 5% headline advantages remain unreconciled. These problems affect the principal additions, making the net quality benefit uncertain.
